findings.stemStart: Regional Bourgogne may be grown almost anywhere in
findings.problem: Explanation contrasted the escarpment with 'the flat land beyond the motorway' carrying 'the same three words'; regional Bourgogne in the Cote d'Or lies mostly between the D974 and the A31, not beyond the motorway, and the real contrast before 2017 was with Bourgogne from anywhere else in the region.
findings.fix: Now reads: a Bourgogne grown on the escarpment had no way of saying so, while one grown anywhere else in the region carried exactly the same name.
findings.source: Bourgogne Cote d'Or DGC (2017) geography; regional Bourgogne covers the whole region

findings.stemStart: Burgundian growers still size a plot in an
findings.problem: Arithmetic wrong: an ouvree is about 4.28 ares, so a hectare holds about 23.3 ouvrees, not 'something like twenty-four'.
findings.fix: Now: 'and a hectare holds a little over twenty-three of them'.
findings.source: 1 ouvree = 428.5 square metres; 10,000 / 428.5 = 23.3

findings.stemStart: Dry transverse valleys cut back into the Cote
findings.problem: Explanation said cold air alone makes ground at a combe mouth 'usually' village land; the usual explanation is mainly the gravel outwash fan, and 'usually' overstated it (premier crus lie on combe flanks, as at Gevrey).
findings.fix: Now: the cold air draining out, and the gravel they have washed down, help explain why the ground at a combe mouth is often village land.
findings.source: Cote d'Or geomorphology: alluvial cones at combe mouths

findings.stemStart: Inside the Vougeot commune a walled premier cru
findings.problem: ex=True list refused La Vigne Blanche, the climat's standard alternative name, so a correct student was marked wrong.
findings.fix: Added 'la vigne blanche' (normalises to 'vigne blanche'). Probed: La Vigne Blanche and vigne blanche grade; Clos de Vougeot and Vougeot still do not.
findings.source: Vougeot premier cru Le Clos Blanc / La Vigne Blanche, the same monopole

findings.fix: Now: 'is routinely ranked alongside the grand crus it was passed over for'.
findings.source: House rule: nothing volatile stated as fact

findings.stemStart: Tucked in a valley behind the Montrachet hill,
findings.problem: Explanation said En Remilly and Murgers des Dents de Chien 'run right up to the Chevalier-Montrachet boundary', a precise adjacency that is not safe for En Remilly, and called the side valley 'the whole reason' for the price.
findings.fix: Now: they 'lie within a short walk of Montrachet and Chevalier-Montrachet', and the side valley is 'much of the reason'.
findings.source: Saint-Aubin premier cru map; softened to what is certainly true

findings.stemStart: Pinot Gris survives in old Burgundian plantings under
findings.problem: Explanation said Pinot Gris is permitted in 'several white appellations'; its common legal place is as an accessory grape in reds (up to 15 percent), and in whites only in some (Coteaux Bourguignons and a few others).
findings.fix: Now: 'the rules still allow it in small amounts, as an accessory grape in many reds as well as in some whites'.

findings.stemStart: A guest compares two vintages of one classified
findings.problem: Key was visibly the longest option (121 characters against a runner-up of 90), a length giveaway.
findings.fix: Key trimmed to 'Each year's selection for the grand vin, set by how each variety fared that season' (81); the qualification moved into exp as its opening sentence. No option is now ten clear of the runner-up.
findings.source: README length rule: trim the key, move the qualification into exp

findings.stemStart: Growers in one Jura appellation submit their wine
findings.problem: Explanation said the wine 'spends more than six years in cask'; the rule is at least 60 months under veil with bottling no earlier than about six years and three months after harvest, so the cask time is overstated. The 'work long since done' clause also assumed the refusal comes after ageing.
findings.fix: Now: 'may not be bottled until more than six years after the harvest, most of that time in cask under a veil of yeast, so a refused year costs its growers dearly'.
findings.source: Vin jaune rules: 60 months under veil, release from 15 December of the sixth year after harvest

findings.stemStart: A Napa estate founded as a Franco-American partnership
findings.problem: Explanation said blending several years 'into one red is ordinary in Champagne' (Champagne is not red), and stated as current that the wine is 'sold largely at the winery', a distribution fact that drifts.
findings.fix: Now 'into one wine', and 'It was long sold only at the winery'.
findings.source: Overture's history as a cellar-door multi-vintage wine; house rule on volatile facts

findings.stemStart: A Saint-Emilion first growth and a Mendoza estate
findings.problem: Cheval Blanc withdrew from the Saint-Emilion classification in 2021 and is no longer a classified first growth, so the stem stated a fact that has changed.
findings.fix: Stem now: 'A Saint-Emilion estate famed for its Cabernet Franc and a Mendoza estate share a Malbec-led red grown on stony Andean ground at around a thousand metres. Name that wine.' Similarity re-run: 0 flagged.
findings.source: Cheval Blanc and Ausone withdrew from the 2022 Saint-Emilion classification (announced 2021)

findings.stemStart: A Saint-Emilion first growth and a Mendoza estate
findings.problem: Explanation called Cabernet Sauvignon 'the Bordeaux partner's contribution' (Cheval Blanc is a Cabernet Franc and Merlot estate), and claimed cuttings of that quality 'no longer exist' in the homeland, an overstatement.
findings.fix: Now: 'a Bordeaux-style blend built on a grape Argentina had long bottled on its own', and old ungrafted vines 'are rare in the variety's French homeland'.
findings.source: Cheval Blanc's planting; Mendoza ungrafted Malbec

findings.source: Cooperage: demi-muid staves are thicker than a barrique's

findings.problem: Key said each name gathers 'the vineyards of many villages', but both Grosslagen gather the sites of essentially one village (Zell with Merl and Kaimt; Kroev), as the explanation itself says. The key was also a length standout (62 against 48).

findings.stemStart: One Mosel collective name was the reverse of
findings.problem: Explanation dated Badstube's conversion to a single vineyard to 2025; the sources found already treat Badstube as an Einzellage before then (VDP lists it as a Grosse Lage, which the VDP grants only to single sites, with 2020-vintage Grosse Lage bottlings; a 2023 estate report calls it one of its Einzellagen), so the year is unsupported and is the kind of recent date the module rules out.
findings.fix: Now: 'the collective has since been dissolved and the name remade as a single vineyard', with no year.
findings.source: vdp.de vineyard page 4010 Badstube; estate vintage reports (WebSearch)
